extraction.name: CommonsenseQA
extraction.description: A challenging dataset for commonsense question answering containing 12,247 multiple-choice questions. Questions are generated by crowd-workers based on ConceptNet concepts, requiring prior knowledge and complex semantics to discriminate between answer choices.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created through a multi-step process: (1) subgraphs were extracted from ConceptNet with one source concept and three target concepts, (2) crowd-workers authored multiple-choice questions that mention the source concept and discriminate between target concepts, (3) crowd-workers filtered questions by quality, (4) crowd-workers added distractors (one from ConceptNet and one authored themselves), and (5) relevant snippets were collected via search engine. The process resulted in 12,247 questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data source is ConceptNet, a commonsense knowledge base. Subgraphs were extracted from ConceptNet, each containing one source concept and three target concepts connected by semantic relations. Additional context snippets were collected via search engine.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd-workers were asked to author multiple-choice questions that mention the source concept and discriminate in turn between each of the target concepts. This encourages workers to create questions with complex semantics that often require prior knowledge. Question formulators were instructed to create questions with high language variation. Crowdworkers also filter questions by quality and add distractors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Analysis of 100 randomly sampled examples from development set to annotate types of commonsense skills needed. Multiple commonsense skills allowed per question. Analysis of question formulation patterns showing 44% start with WH-words, 5% use first names for context, 7% use 'if' for hypothetical questions. Analysis of commonsense skill categories including Spatial (41%), Cause & Effect (23%), Has parts (23%), Is member of (17%), Purpose (18%), Social (15%), Activity (8%), Definition (6%), and Preconditions (3%).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 122 formulators contributed to question generation. However, 10 workers formulated more than 85% of the questions.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: CONCEPTNET knowledge base was used to extract subgraphs with source and target concepts. Search engine was used to collect relevant snippets.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for commonsense question answering tasks, with questions that require prior knowledge and complex semantics. The dataset can be used for training and evaluating natural language understanding systems.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions are filtered through a verification process where each question is verified by 2 workers, and only questions verified by at least one worker that answered correctly are used. This process filters out 15% of the questions. Additionally, triplets are filtered based on multiple criteria: general relations are removed, concepts must be 4 words or less and in English, and edit distance between concepts must be sufficiently high.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data preprocessing involves filtering ConceptNet triplets through multiple steps: (1) filtering triplets with general relations or well-explored relations, using 22 relations total; (2) filtering triplets where concepts are more than four words or not in English; (3) filtering triplets where edit distance between concepts is too low. This results in 236,208 triplets from an initial 32 million. Question sets are then created by grouping three triplets with the same question concept and relation.
